reference.source: Firestein & Kelley's Textbook of Rheumatology / Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine
clinicalPearls: A rare non-Langerhans histiocytosis causing a destructive polyarthritis together with characteristic skin and mucosal papules and nodules
The arthritis is typically symmetrical and can rapidly progress to a mutilating, resorptive deformity (arthritis mutilans)
Firm, reddish-brown papulonodules cluster around the nail folds ('coral bead' sign) and over the hands, face, and ears
It is a recognised paraneoplastic association, so a search for occult malignancy is essential at diagnosis
Associations also include autoimmune disease, hyperlipidaemia, and a positive tuberculin response in some patients
Histology shows infiltration by multinucleated giant cells and histiocytes with abundant eosinophilic 'ground-glass' cytoplasm
Treatment combines systemic immunosuppression, sometimes with bisphosphonates and TNF or other biologic agents, to halt joint destruction
reference.pathophysiology: Multicentric reticulohistiocytosis is a systemic histiocytic disorder in which histiocytes and multinucleated giant cells with characteristic ground-glass eosinophilic cytoplasm infiltrate the synovium, skin, and other tissues. Overexpression of proinflammatory cytokines, particularly tumour necrosis factor and interleukin-1 and interleukin-6, and osteoclast-activating pathways (including RANK ligand signalling) drives the aggressive, erosive joint destruction. The infiltrating cells are of monocyte-macrophage lineage. The frequent association with malignancy and autoimmune disease suggests an aberrant reactive immune process rather than a purely clonal neoplasm.
additionalDifferentials: Gout and other crystal arthropathies with tophi
additionalInvestigations: Skin or synovial biopsy showing giant cells and histiocytes with ground-glass eosinophilic cytoplasm
Radiographs of affected joints demonstrating well-marginated erosions and joint destruction
Inflammatory markers and autoimmune serology to assess associated conditions
Fasting lipid profile given the association with hyperlipidaemia
Age-appropriate malignancy screening given the paraneoplastic association
redFlags: Rapidly progressive joint destruction threatening arthritis mutilans
Features suggesting an underlying occult malignancy
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss and fever prompting malignancy evaluation
reference.prognosis: The skin lesions may eventually regress, but untreated joint disease can progress rapidly to severe, disabling arthritis mutilans; overall outlook is heavily influenced by any associated malignancy.
pitfalls: Mistaking it for rheumatoid or psoriatic arthritis and missing the diagnostic skin nodules
Failing to screen for an underlying malignancy
Delaying aggressive treatment and allowing irreversible joint destruction
Attributing the nodules to gouty tophi without biopsy
management: Immunosuppression with corticosteroids combined with a disease-modifying agent such as methotrexate, with leflunomide or cyclophosphamide for resistant disease
Biologic therapy targeting tumour necrosis factor, and bisphosphonates to inhibit the osteoclast and RANK-ligand-driven bone destruction, in refractory or aggressive arthritis
Investigate for and treat any associated occult malignancy, given the paraneoplastic association
Symptomatic joint care with analgesia and physiotherapy to preserve function
Screen for and manage associated hyperlipidaemia and autoimmune disease
Monitor joint radiographs and function to detect progression towards arthritis mutilans and to guide treatment intensification
